title: Families of Faith
objective: After this level you can sort the world's religions into the Abrahamic, Indian, East Asian and Indigenous families and say what links each family.
summary: The Abrahamic faiths share Abraham; the Indian family shares karma and rebirth; East Asian traditions blend and honor ancestors; Indigenous traditions are many, each tied to its people and place.

cards.headline: Religions have family trees, too.
cards.body: Sorting them into families shows who shares an ancestor, an idea or a homeland. Here are four families, and a warning about the last one.

cards.headline: The Abrahamic family
cards.body: Judaism, Christianity and Islam share reverence for Abraham, who is often considered the first monotheist. They trace the family line differently: Jews and Christians through his son Isaac, Muslims through his son Ishmael. Three faiths, one ancestor.

cards.headline: The Indian family
cards.body: Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism all began in the Indian subcontinent, Sikhism in the Punjab in the late 15th century. Running through much of this family is karma, the law by which good or bad actions shape future existence, together with rebirth (samsara) and the hope of release from it (moksha).

cards.headline: The East Asian family
cards.body: In China, religion draws on Confucianism, Daoism and Buddhism, often blended with folk traditions; in Japan, Shinto is the indigenous religion. Remember Level 2's Confucian scholar at a Daoist ritual? East Asians, Britannica notes, may call themselves Shintoists, Daoists, Buddhists or Christians, yet seldom stop being Confucians. Honoring ancestors is widespread: in a 2023 survey, roughly half or more of adults everywhere surveyed had made them offerings in the past year.
cards.callout: Linked by: blending traditions, honoring ancestors

cards.headline: Indigenous traditions: many, not one
cards.body: Here's the warning. There is no single "Native American religion". Practices differ from people to people, are often tied to particular places, and are passed on orally. The Menominee, for instance, explain their origins through the geography of their own homeland. "Indigenous" names many traditions, each belonging to its own people and land.

The Indian family shares karma, rebirth and release
East Asian traditions blend; Indigenous traditions are many, not one
